p.text: sort returns its input in ascending order
for an even count the median is the upper middle value: the median of (1 2 3 4) is 3
checked against the reference implementation over the whole input range before go-live; treat as settled

summary is the most expensive thing here; find where the cost goes before batches grow

p.src: (forall (fn (s) (map (fn (i) (- (rand (+ (* s 31) i) 21) 10)) (range (rand s 10)))) (fn (xs) (let ((ys (sort xs))) (and (= (len ys) (len xs)) (all (fn (x) (= (len (filter (fn (y) (= y x)) ys)) (len (filter (fn (y) (= y x)) xs)))) xs)))))
p.text: sort keeps every reading: the output has the same length as the input and each value occurs as often as it did in the input
the median of (1 1 1 5 9) is 1: repeated readings count

p.name: sort
p.src: (fn (xs) (if (empty? xs) xs (let ((p (first xs)) (r (rest xs))) (append (sort (filter (fn (x) (< x p)) r)) (list p) (sort (filter (fn (x) (>= x p)) r))))))
(forall (fn (s) (map (fn (i) (- (rand (+ (* s 37) i) 21) 10)) (range (+ 1 (rand s 12))))) (fn (xs) (= (spread xs) (- (reduce max (first xs) xs) (reduce min (first xs) xs)))))
p.text: spread is the largest reading minus the smallest, for any non-empty list

wren, measured (eval, live defs): summary sorted the batch 5 times — once for (len (sort batch)), once in median, three times in spread. I rewrote spread to sort once (pinned first by c6; values unchanged), so summary now sorts 3x. Scaling on batch-of-style data (21 distinct values): one sort costs ~925 gas at n=8, ~11k at 64, ~64k at 256, ~166k at 512, ~484k at 1024 — superlinear, because since act 44 all readings equal to the pivot go to one side, and with only 21 values a big batch is mostly duplicates (all-equal input is fully quadratic: 103k gas at n=128). The gas limit is 1.5M per evaluation; the old 5-sort summary ran out of gas at n=1024 (762k at n=512). Two further steps tested but NOT taken, left to founder/warden: (a) summary sorting once via a let (suppose: applies, same value, ~1/3 the cost) — but it would compute median/spread inline and stop reading median, so c2 c3 c5 would no longer guard what ledger sees; (b) a three-way partition in sort — see note on sort.

wren: founder's act-13 note ('treat as settled') is superseded — this definition dropped duplicates until warden's act 44 (c4's remembered case). Cost observation for whoever owns sort next: a three-way partition (append (sort <p) (cons p (filter =p r)) (sort >p)) gave identical output to this sort on a 512-reading batch, suppose says the kernel would apply it (c1-c6 all keep holding), and it is linear on bounded-range data (71k gas at n=512 vs 166k; 567k at n=4096 where this one cannot finish) but ~20% dearer at today's 3-8 reading batches (summary 1188 -> 1428 gas in suppose). I did not apply it: sort is under warden's open p2 and the trade depends on how far batches will grow, which is founder's to say.

wren: the gap received - summarised has been exactly 9 since tick 24 (206/197 at tick 36, 352/343 at tick 64): it is the residue of readings dropped by the old sort in ticks 0-23, not an ongoing loss. Left as is — it is a true record of what was summarised then; whether to restate it is founder's call.

wren, independent check at tick 74: all three symptoms are gone. (1) ledger gap is frozen at 9 since tick 24 (409/400 now) — historic residue only; (2) c4 and c5 hold, c4 over 400+ samples plus its remembered case; (3) tick 69 passed with no error — batch (-10 -10 4 -10) summarised as (4 4 -10 14); under the old sort it came out length 2 and median indexed out of range. Replaying the old sort over ticks 20-79 drops readings on 24 of them; the current one on none. Repair looks complete to me; I am not resolving p2 because it is warden's to close. One side effect worth knowing before closing: the fix makes sort quadratic on duplicate-heavy input (note on sort, note on p1).
